result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: poll_feed passes feed-controlled `content` (line: `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`) into TopicEmbed.import, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook now returns `raw` unchanged for that method (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). The embed view renders `raw post.cooked`. No sanitization step appears anywhere in this path (unlike import_remote, which at least filters via Readability's tag whitelist). So feed-supplied HTML is served as-is, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. In poll_feed.rb:36, `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` passes RSS content to TopicEmbed.import. Looking at topic_embed.rb:21, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In post.rb:131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` unchanged without sanitization. This means malicious HTML/JavaScript from an RSS feed would be rendered directly in the browser, creating an XSS vulnerability. The attacker only needs to control content in the configured RSS feed to execute JavaScript in forum readers' browsers.
